title: Prefill/decode scheduling inversion and softmax rounding skew
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production can return subtly different token probabilities after a recent scheduler/attention optimization. Root cause appears tied to an inversion of prefill vs decode kernel arbitration under high concurrency which changes micro-batching alignment and causes reproducible softmax rounding skew for some model shapes. Outputs deviate enough to fail deterministic evals for a small subset of prompt sets.
repro_steps: Deploy the scheduler branch with preemption heuristic X enabled (ref: draft PR) on a 4-GPU pool.
Run the model\"molten-3b\" with long-prefill workloads (prefill length ~1024) while concurrently issuing low-latency decode requests that trigger preemption.
Collect token probability traces across identical requests with and without the scheduler toggle and compare softmax outputs for last 16 tokens.
Observe consistent KL divergence of 1e-5 to 1e-4 and small token swaps in beam-ranking for ~0.5% of cases.
investigation_notes: 2025-09-13 - Initial report from nightly-evals by SRE: non-deterministic eval failures after deploying scheduler improvement.
2025-09-14 - Reproduced locally on a 4xA100 staging pool. Attn kernels differ in ordering when prefill batches are split across devices.

2025-09-15 - Added logging to kernel selection path: found that arbitration policy sometimes prefers a decode-optimized kernel during remaining prefill ops due to stale priority tokens in the scheduler queue.
2025-09-16 - Verified that numerical differences disappear when forcing strict prefill-first scheduling (no decode preemption).
2025-09-18 - Experimented with increasing softmax accumulator precision in fallback kernels; reduced drift but did not eliminate ordering-dependent differences.

2025-09-20 - Discovered a race in the per-request KV-index promotion path: simultaneous handoff of cached KV slices can reorder memory writes under preemption, causing tiny accumulation ordering changes in fused attention math.
2025-09-22 - Benchmarked impact: enabling strict ordering increases p95 latency by ~6% for mixed workloads; unit cost increases marginally.
root_cause: Scheduler arbitration allows decode-optimized kernels to preempt remaining prefill shards. This changes the micro-batch composition sent to fused-attention kernels and, combined with non-associative FP32 summation in the softmax exponent accumulators and a race in KV slice promotion, produces small but measurable numerical drift and token-ranking changes.
proposed_fix: Immediate: revert the preemption heuristic for prefill-active requests to enforce prefill-before-decode on the same logical request (short-term patch).
Short-term: add a lightweight ordering fence in KV slice promotion to ensure deterministic memory write ordering when preemption is allowed.

Medium-term: refactor scheduler to annotate batch fragments with execution-stability flags and prefer stable ordering for requests marked as deterministic-sensitive (e.g., evals, customers with reproducibility SLAs).
Long-term: add configurable higher-precision accumulation in fused-softmax and/or deterministic reduction paths that can be toggled per-model or per-route.
Add a regression test suite that runs mixed prefill/decode workloads across kernel variants to catch ordering-induced drift early.
deploy_plan: Run internal staged rollout: canary on runtime-1.20-staging pool for 24h with nightly-evals enabled
If canary passes, roll to production with 10%->50%->100% traffic ramp over 48h
Monitor evals: token KL divergence, deterministic eval pass-rate, latency P50/P95, and batch throughput
If regressions persist, hotfix to re-enable strict ordering fences and rollback scheduler heuristic changes.
tests: Unit: scheduler arbitration unit tests covering preemption cases (new test vectors added)
Integration: 4xA100 mixed prefill/decode scenarii reproducer in CI (deterministic seed), comparing PR runs to baseline
E2E: nightly-evals with long-prefill promptset and deterministic token-trace diff checker
Performance: benchmark suite measuring p50/p95 with/without ordering fence and with forced high-precision accumulation
